The function \( f \) is odd, so \( f(-x) = -f(x) \). The function \( g \) is even, so \( g(-x) = g(x) \). We evaluate the composition from the inside out:

1. Innermost: \( f(x) \) is odd.
2. \( g(f(x)) \): \( g \) is even, so \( g(\text{odd}) = \text{even} \).
3. \( f(g(f(x))) \): \( f \) is odd, so \( f(\text{even}) = \text{even} \).
4. \( g(f(g(f(x)))) \): \( g \) is even, so \( g(\text{even}) = \text{even} \).
5. \( f(g(f(g(f(x))))) \): \( f \) is odd, so \( f(\text{even}) = \text{even} \).
6. Outermost: \( f(\text{even}) = \text{even} \).

Once an even function is applied, all subsequent compositions remain even. Therefore, the entire composition is even.

Answer: even
